summary: The submission is a polished, successfully rendered 3D beach scene with a clearly recognizable pelican riding a bicycle. The camera framing responds to horizontal pointer movement, the rider/bike remain readable over time, desktop and 390px-wide layouts both render without page overflow, and a reload recovers the scene. The only diagnostics issue observed was a nonblocking favicon 404.

runtime.reason: The page loaded with its title and fully rendered scene, and rendered again after reload. Its canvas uses WebGL 2.0. The network capture shows the page and both Three.js module requests returning 200; the sole console error is a nonblocking missing favicon.ico.

scene.reason: A full-viewport WebGL canvas shows genuine depth, modeled geometry, occlusion and directional shadows. Pointer-driven framing changes reveal foreground/midground/background parallax rather than a static image.

checks.reason: Three distinct desktop views, plus the mobile view, show coherent 3D geometry: the bicycle frame and spoked wheels occupy depth, the pelican occludes the bicycle and background, and the castle, palm, bike and shoreline shift with parallax while maintaining consistent relative placement. Cast shadows reinforce the spatial layout.

The composition has clear hierarchy: the legible title sits against open sky while the pelican and bicycle command the center. Warm sand, turquoise water, bright sun, soft shadows, matte materials and restrained accent colors form a coherent sunny-beach expression at both tested widths.

Moving the pointer horizontally across the canvas produced a clear, meaningful spatial response: the camera framing and foreground layout changed smoothly. No buttons, links or other controls were advertised, so no extra controls were invented.

The pointer-driven view changes were repeatable in both directions, including returning to the left-side view after the right-side view. Reloading restored the complete scene rather than leaving a partial or failed state. There were no requested undo, pause or gameplay flows to exercise.

At 1440x900 and 390x844 the canvas filled the viewport exactly and document scroll width matched the viewport, with no page overflow. The pelican, bicycle and bottom status badge remained readable on mobile; the decorative left sandcastle is partially cropped at 390px. Reload succeeded. Tab left focus on BODY because there are no focusable controls. Diagnostics contain only the nonblocking favicon 404; main resources returned 200.

The central subject is unmistakably a pelican, with a white body, large orange bill and pouch, wing, eye and hat. It sits over a recognizable bicycle with two spoked wheels, a diamond-like frame, handlebars, saddle, pedals and basket, inside a genuine 3D beach scene.

Sunny beach conditions are immediately apparent from the bright sun, warm sand, turquoise water and beach props. The straw hat, flowers, slow cruise title, low tide timestamp and relaxed seated pose establish a leisurely presentation.

The pelican, bicycle and shore remain readable in left, right and mobile views. Repeated observations over time show smooth, coherent idle/camera motion without broken silhouettes or the subject leaving the readable composition.

instruction.reason: All stated visible requirements are delivered coherently: a pelican riding a bicycle, a sunny beach, and a relaxed single-page presentation. No requested flow is missing or contradictory.

spatial.reason: Recognizable modeled forms, convincing scale relationships, depth cues, occlusion, shadows and pointer-dependent parallax consistently serve the scene across multiple views. No material or connection defect materially breaks the intended subject.

interaction.reason: The supplied pointer-driven camera response works reliably and reverses naturally, but it has no visible cue, cursor change or control affordance to tell users the scene is interactive. That is a local discoverability issue rather than a broken flow.

visual.reason: Composition, typography, color, lighting and 3D form are cohesive and purposeful. The centered subject remains legible against the low-detail background, while secondary props add depth and a relaxed beach mood without competing with the rider.

stability.reason: Desktop, narrow viewport, resizing and reload all remained readable and reliable. Main assets loaded successfully and the only console defect was an unrelated favicon 404; no crash, freeze or blocking resource failure was observed.

limitations: No explicit buttons, links, form controls, focusable elements, download/export action or pause/undo control were present; Tab focus remained on BODY, so those non-requested flows had nothing valid to exercise.
Real touch hardware, audio quality and internal Three.js implementation details were not evaluated from browser observations; no audio control was presented.
At 390x844 the decorative sandcastle is partially cropped by the left viewport edge, while the pelican, bicycle and bottom status badge remain readable and reachable.
Console and network diagnostics are saved in evidence/console.txt and evidence/network.txt; they are reported here rather than cited as visual evidence.
